problem_summary.summary: Determine whether the letters in one string can be selected from a second string, using each available letter no more than once.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: lowercase strings ransomNote and magazine. Return true if magazine has enough copies of every needed letter; otherwise return false.
constraints: Both strings contain lowercase English letters

brute_force.explanation: For each note character, scan magazine for an equal unused position and mark that position used. A missing match makes construction impossible.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Each successful match reserves a distinct magazine position, so the process succeeds exactly when every requested character has a separate available copy.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(r * m) worst case, where r and m are the note and magazine lengths.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(m) auxiliary for tracking used magazine positions.

optimized.explanation: Count magazine letters in a 26-entry array, then consume one count for each note letter; fail as soon as a count is zero.
optimized.correctness_idea: The count array records the exact available multiplicity of every lowercase letter. Decrementing once per requested occurrence enforces the one-use limit and succeeds iff all demands are met.
optimized.time_complexity: O(r + m), where r and m are the input lengths.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary: the 26 counters have fixed size.

steps.condition: Each magazine position contributes one copy.
steps.action: Finish the pass with a:2 and b:1; other counts are zero.
Decrement a; all note characters were supplied, so return true.

edge_cases.handling: Its count is zero when consumed, so false is returned immediately.

edge_cases.case: The note needs more copies than available
edge_cases.handling: Each occurrence decrements the count; the first overdraw returns false.
Unused counts do not affect success.
